statement_source_and_scope_match: S12 Conjecture 1.3 asks for a polynomial in n alone; n>=d+1 makes this equivalent to an absolute polynomial bound in n+d. BX26 §1 and W25 §I explicitly use dimension and facet count. Bounded, full-dimensional representation loses no bounded polytope after passage to its affine hull. Vertices/edges/facets and graph distance agree with T14 and S19.
proposed_statement_text:
A convex polytope $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a bounded intersection of finitely many closed half-spaces. Assume $P$ has nonempty interior in $\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge1$, and exactly $n$ facets, its faces of dimension $d-1$. In particular, $n\ge d+1$.

The vertex-edge graph $G(P)$ has the vertices of $P$ as its nodes; two nodes are adjacent precisely when they are the endpoints of an edge of $P$. For vertices $u,v$, let $\operatorname{dist}_{G(P)}(u,v)$ be the minimum number of edges in a path joining them. Define

$$
\operatorname{diam}G(P)=\max_{u,v\in V(P)}\operatorname{dist}_{G(P)}(u,v).
$$

Do there exist absolute constants $C,k>0$ such that every such polytope satisfies

$$
\operatorname{diam}G(P)\le C(n+d)^k?
$$

The same constants must work for all dimensions and all facet counts. There are no rationality, simplicity or conditioning assumptions. Paths use actual edges and may move in either direction; no linear objective is prescribed. This is the polynomial Hirsch conjecture for bounded polytopes. It asks for the existence of short paths, without requiring an algorithm to find them.
applied_significance: A bounded feasible region in linear programming is a polytope, and nondegenerate simplex pivots move between its vertices along edges. Its graph diameter therefore gives a geometric lower bound on the worst-case number of pivots needed when the starting vertex and objective vary. A superpolynomial diameter family would obstruct every uniformly polynomial pivot bound. A polynomial diameter bound would remove that obstruction, while leaving the additional tasks of choosing objective-improving steps and computing them efficiently. These extra algorithmic requirements are the subject of existing [entry 100](../../../problems/100-strongly-polynomial-simplex.md); the present question concerns the geometry of the feasible region.

later_results_and_resolution_checks.comparison: Same undirected bounded model, but counterexample defeats n-d; linear lower-bound family is compatible with higher polynomial bounds. The paper explicitly retains the polynomial conjecture.
Dimension d+1, (2d+1)(d+1)+1 facets, every coherent monotone path >=2^(d-1)-1. Extra coherence and prescribed objective restrict admissible paths; candidate minimizes over all undirected edge paths.
Ax=b, x>=0, rank(A)=m; maximal steps along support-minimal kernel vectors may cross interior and reach nonvertices. O(m² log m) therefore bounds a relaxation of edge paths, not G(P).

Pi_2^p-complete decision of whether diameter<=input t for bipartite perfect-matching polytopes. Even these 0/1 polytopes satisfy small diameter bounds, so exact-value hardness does not imply superpolynomial diameter.
All n>=d>=2, but exponent log_2 g(d) grows like log_2 d-log_2 log d+O(1). It is not a universal constant; no polynomial Hirsch resolution.

Theorem 1.1 restricts to objective-increasing paths, while ordinary diameter in the same integer box is <=18d by the recalled lattice bound. Theorem 1.2 concerns unbounded polyhedra and measures exponential growth in dimension without controlling facet count. Both differ from bounded undirected diameter polynomial in n+d.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Requests a computable deterministic monotone simplex pivot rule on rational LPs with bit-length and auxiliary-operation bounds. Here the assertion is existence of undirected short paths for every real bounded polytope; it gives no rule, objective monotonicity or cost for discovering paths.
Carrying simplex concerns regularity of a dynamical invariant hypersurface; the shared word simplex has no mathematical equivalence.
Arithmetic circuits are symbolic computation DAGs; circuit walks in the scope checks here are geometric kernel directions. No common assertion.

implications_or_equivalences: Polynomial in n and d is equivalent to polynomial in n for bounded d-polytopes with n facets.
The exact linear, monotone, strict monotone and coherent variants are not counted as additional entries.
Small undirected diameter alone does not produce an efficient objective-improving pivot algorithm.
